items.name: Relative curve
items.statement: A relative curve X→S is projective and flat of pure relative dimension one, with geometrically connected fibers. It has genus g when every geometric fiber has arithmetic genus g.
items.note: The paper’s terminology is fiberwise; see the separate nodal/semistable convention and self-node correction in the appended items and report. Existing nodal/relative-curve owner, with the documented terminology bridge.

items.name: Maximal variation
items.statement: For a smooth relative genus-g>1 curve over a quasi-projective integral S over a noetherian ring R, maximal variation means the classifying map S→M_{g,R} is generically finite: its restriction to some dense open of S is quasi-finite.
items.note: Extracted from the stated author-manuscript locator; status and route are provisional in this partial checkpoint.

items.name: Relative powers
items.statement: For X→S define X^m_{/S} as the m-fold fiber product for m>0 and X^0_{/S}=S.
items.note: Use common scheme fiber products and the line-bundle pullback/tensor API; the adelic extension is supplied separately.

items.name: Model adelic divisor group
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. For a projective integral model X containing U as an open subscheme set Divhat(X,U)=Divhat(X)_Q ×_{Div(U)_Q} Div(U), and Divhat(U/k)_mod=colim_X Divhat(X,U), with transition pullbacks. For k=Z, Divhat means arithmetic Cartier divisors with continuous Green functions; for a field it means ordinary Cartier divisors. A model divisor is effective if it has an effective representative.

items.name: Boundary norm and adelic divisor completion
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. Choose a projective model X0 and strictly effective arithmetic boundary E0 whose underlying support is X0\U. Define ||D||_{E0}=inf{epsilon in Q_{>0}: -epsilon E0≤D≤epsilon E0}, allowing infinity. Divhat(U/k) is the completion of model adelic divisors in this boundary topology. A representative Cauchy sequence has |D_j-D_i|≤epsilon_i E0 for j≥i, epsilon_i→0; its underlying integral Cartier divisor on U is constant.

items.name: Independence of the boundary topology
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. The topology on Divhat(U/k)_mod defined by the boundary norm is independent of the chosen projective boundary (X0,E0).
items.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, §2.1, p.18, recalled from [YZ2] §2.2

items.name: Rational hermitian line-bundle groupoid
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. On a projective model X, a rational hermitian line bundle is a pair (a,L) with a rational and L a hermitian line bundle (ordinary when k is a field). Morphisms aL→a′L′ form colim_m Isom(amL,a′mL′), over positive denominators making both coefficients integral. Metrics are continuous and morphisms are isometries.

items.name: Adelic line-bundle groupoid
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. An object consists of an integral line bundle L on U, projective models Xi, rational hermitian bundles Li on Xi, and identifications ell_i:L→Li|U in Pic(U)_Q, such that divhat(ell_i ell_1^{-1}) is boundary-Cauchy. A morphism is an isomorphism iota:L→L′ for which divhat(ell′_i iota ell_i^{-1})→0 in the boundary topology. Isomorphism classes form Pichat(U/k); the forgetful functor sends an object to L.

items.name: Divisor presentation of adelic Picard groups
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. The map Divhat(U/k)→Pichat(U/k), D↦O(D), is surjective; its kernel is the image of principal arithmetic divisors on projective models of U.

items.name: Effective adelic divisors and bundles
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. An adelic divisor is effective if it is a boundary limit of effective model arithmetic divisors of mixed coefficients. An adelic line-bundle class is effective if it lies in the image of an effective adelic divisor.

items.name: Strong nefness
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. An adelic divisor or bundle is strongly nef if it is represented by a boundary-convergent sequence of nef arithmetic model divisors or hermitian model line bundles, respectively. For a field, use ordinary nef model objects.

items.name: Nef adelic bundles
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. An adelic divisor or bundle L is nef if there is a strongly nef M such that aL+M is strongly nef for every positive integer a.

items.name: Integrable adelic bundles
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. An adelic divisor or bundle is integrable if it is the difference of two strongly nef objects. Write Pichat(U/k)_int for the resulting subgroup, and Picboldhat(U/k)_int for the full subgroupoid.

items.name: Global Berkovich analytification
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. Glue the spaces M(A) of multiplicative seminorms on affine coordinate rings A of U; when k is a field require seminorms trivial on k. Use the coarsest topology making affine charts open and evaluations v↦|f|_v continuous. Each point v has a completed residue field H_v. This gives U^an=(U/k)^an.

items.name: Topology of global analytification
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. The space (U/k)^an is Hausdorff, path-connected and locally compact.

items.name: Analytic arithmetic divisor
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. An arithmetic divisor on U^an is (D,g_D), where D is a Cartier divisor on U and g_D is continuous on U^an\|D|^an, such that g_D+log|f| extends continuously over V^an whenever D|V=div(f). The convention uses log|f|, not twice that function.

items.name: Continuous metrized line bundle
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. A metrized bundle on U^an is an algebraic line bundle L on U with a continuously varying norm on the one-dimensional H_v-vector space L⊗H_v at every v∈U^an. Morphisms are algebraic isomorphisms preserving every norm.

items.name: Injective divisor analytification
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. The natural map Divhat(U/k)→Divhat(U^an) is injective.

Limits of projective Deligne pairings define f_*<L1,...,L_{n+1}> as an integrable adelic line bundle on V for integrable adelic L_i on U, functorially in the bundle groupoids.

items.name: Effective sections and adelic h0
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. For an adelic L define Hhat^0(U,L)={s∈H^0(U,L_underlying):||s(x)||≤1 for all x∈U^an}. If k=Z this set is finite and hhat^0 is log of its cardinality; over a field it is a finite-dimensional k-vector space and hhat^0 is its dimension.

items.name: Adelic volume and bigness
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. For d=dim U define volhat(U,L)=lim_{m→∞} d! hhat^0(U,mL)/m^d. A bundle is big if this volume is strictly positive.

items.name: Existence of the adelic volume limit
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. For every adelic line bundle L the limit defining volhat(U,L) exists as a finite real number.

items.name: Adelic Hilbert–Samuel formula
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. If L is nef and d=dim U, then volhat(U,L)=L^d; consequently such L is big iff its top self-intersection is positive.

items.name: Adelic objects over a global field
items.statement: Let either k=Z, K a number field and B=Spec O_K, or k a field and K the function field of a regular projective k-curve B. For a quasi-projective K-variety X take direct limits of adelic divisors, Picard groups and bundle groupoids over flat quasi-projective integral B-models U with X open in U_K. An isomorphism over X represents an adelic isomorphism if it extends with its metric on a common open model. Effectivity, nefness, integrability, analytification and intersection descend through these limits.

items.name: Global-field adelic volume
items.statement: In the preceding global-field setting, effective sections of an adelic L on X, defined by ||s(x)||≤1 on (X/k)^an, have finite logarithmic count for k=Z or finite k-dimension otherwise. With d=dim X+1, lim_m d! hhat^0(X,mL)/m^d exists; for nef L it equals the adelic intersection L^d.

items.name: Descent of fiberwise constant adelic metrics
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field. All schemes below are flat quasi-projective integral k-schemes. Let pi:X→S be projective flat with geometrically connected fibers; assume S normal or pi has a section. Let barL be integrable with underlying L≅pi^*M. Suppose on each X_{H_v}, v∈S^an, the metric is a constant multiple of the trivial metric induced by M. Then M has an integrable adelic extension barM with pi^*barM≅barL.

items.name: Deligne pairing preserves nef bigness

If L1 is effective integrable, L2,...,L_{n+1} nef and M1,...,M_{d-1} nef on V, then f_*<L1,...,L_{n+1}>·M1...M_{d-1}≥0.

items.name: Adelic Siu–Yuan inequality
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field and U a quasi-projective flat integral k-scheme. If A,B are nef adelic bundles and d=dim U, then volhat(A-B)≥A^d-d A^{d-1}·B. In particular, for A nef big and B nef, A-epsilon B has positive volume for sufficiently small positive rational epsilon.

items.name: Composition of adelic Deligne pairings
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field. All schemes below are flat quasi-projective integral k-schemes. Let psi:X→Y and pi:Y→S be projective flat of relative dimensions r and m, with Y,S normal. Let L1,...,L_{r+1} on X and M1,...,M_{m+1} on Y be integrable adelic bundles. There is a canonical isometry (pi psi)_*<L1,...,L_{r+1},psi^*M1,...,psi^*Mm>≅pi_*<psi_*<L1,...,L_{r+1}>,M1,...,Mm>.
items.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, Lemma 2.1–2.2 proofs pp.26–27; [YZ2] Lemma 4.6.1

items.name: Canonical admissible dualizing bundle
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k, and pi:X→S smooth projective with geometrically connected fibers of genus g>0. The relative dualizing bundle admits a unique isomorphism class of adelic extension w whose metric on every X_{H_v}, v∈S^an, is the canonical admissible metric.

items.name: Canonical admissible diagonal bundle
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field, S a quasi-projective flat normal integral k-scheme, and pi:X→S a smooth projective family of geometrically connected curves of genus g>0. For Delta:X→X×_S X, there is a unique isomorphism class of integrable adelic extension D of O(Delta) inducing the canonical admissible metric on every (X_{H_v}^2)^an.

Write w=baromega_{X/S,a} and D=barO(Delta)_a for the canonical admissible bundles and <A,B>=pi_*<A,B> for the adelic Deligne pairing. The canonical algebraic isomorphism omega_{X/S}→Delta^*O(-Delta) is an isometry w→Delta^*(-D).

items.name: Degree-d Abel–Jacobi morphism
items.statement: Let X→S be a smooth projective family of geometrically connected genus-g>0 curves over a noetherian scheme S, J=Pic^0_{X/S}, and alpha a line bundle of relative degree d. The relative Picard functor defines i_alpha:X→J by x↦d[x]-alpha.

items.name: Canonical twice-theta bundle
items.statement: For a smooth relative genus-g>0 curve X→S over noetherian S let J=Pic^0_{X/S}, e:S→J, and P the rigidified Poincare bundle on J×J obtained via the canonical principal polarization. Define Theta=Delta_J^*(P^vee).

items.name: Admissible adelic extension
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field, S a quasi-projective flat normal integral k-scheme, and pi:X→S a smooth projective family of geometrically connected curves of genus g>0. For W=X, X×_S X, or an abelian scheme over S, an integrable adelic extension barL of L on W is admissible if for every v∈S^an its metric on W_{H_v} is admissible in the complete-valued-field sense of Appendix A.

items.name: Existence of admissible extensions

items.name: Uniqueness of admissible extensions modulo base metrics
items.statement: Let k be Z or a field, S flat quasi-projective normal integral over k, and pi:X→S smooth projective with geometrically connected fibers of genus g>0. For W equal to X, X×_S X, or an abelian scheme over S, two admissible integrable adelic extensions of the same algebraic L differ by pi_W^*N, for N∈ker(Pichat(S/k)_int→Pic(S)). Pullback is injective, so the extensions form a torsor under this group.

items.name: Relative algebraically trivial Picard subgroups
items.statement: For a projective flat S-scheme Y define Pic^0(Y) to consist of line bundles algebraically equivalent to zero on every geometric fiber, and Pic^0_{Y/S}(S) as the corresponding subgroup of the relative Picard functor. For Y1,Y2 projective flat over S, Pic^{00}(Y1×_S Y2) consists of bundles algebraically trivial on fibers of each projection.

Let alpha have positive relative degree d and i_alpha:X→J be its Abel map. Under Pic^0_{J/S}≅Pic^0_{X/S}, the map i_alpha^* is multiplication by d.

items.name: Canonical Gross–Schoen cycle
items.statement: Let C/K be smooth projective geometrically connected of genus g>1 over a number field or one-variable function field. Choose a rational degree-one divisor xi=sum a_i p_i representing omega/(2g-2). In CH^2(C^3)_Q define Delta_xi=Delta_123-Delta_12-Delta_23-Delta_31+Delta_1+Delta_2+Delta_3, where Delta_12=sum a_i{(x,x,p_i)}, the other two partial diagonals are permutations, and Delta_1=sum a_i a_j{(x,p_i,p_j)}, with analogous Delta_2,Delta_3. This cycle is homologically trivial.

items.statement: Let k be Z or a field, S a quasi-projective flat normal integral k-scheme, and pi:X→S a smooth projective family of geometrically connected curves of genus g>1 with maximal variation. items.name: Northcott property of the normalized admissible self-intersection
items.statement: Combining the theorem with the Northcott property of the Faltings height, one obtains: for a fixed genus g > 1 and a fixed bound on the degree [K:Q], the invariant omega^2_{C/K,a} has the Northcott property as the smooth projective curve C with everywhere semistable reduction and the number field K both vary. The finiteness is of geometric isomorphism classes, that is of the corresponding points of the coarse moduli space of curves of genus g over Qbar realizable over a field of degree at most the given bound; it is not a statement about isomorphism classes over one fixed K, which would need a separate finiteness-of-twists argument. The two inputs are the Northcott property of Faltings heights of abelian varieties with semistable reduction over number fields, quoted from [FC, Chap. V, Prop. 4.6], and Torelli's theorem, which transfers it to curves.
items.note: Remark 4.15(2). Recorded with the quotient made explicit: as printed, 'satisfies the Northcott property when varying the smooth projective curve C and the number field K' does not say which notion of isomorphism is meant, and the naive fixed-K reading would count one curve once for every field of bounded degree over which it is defined. The geometric reading is the one the cited inputs support, and it is the one Pazuki's theta-height Northcott theorem is stated for. [FC, Chap. V, Prop. 4.6] itself was not read by this session, so the precise form of the quoted input remains an open gap; see the gaps list.

items.name: Relative Bogomolov small-points property
items.statement: Let K be a number field or one-variable function field with arithmetic base k=Z or constant base k, S a quasi-projective normal K-variety, A→S an abelian scheme, and iota:Y→A generically finite. items.name: Arakelov probability form
items.statement: Let C be a compact Riemann surface of genus g>0. For an orthonormal basis alpha_1,...,alpha_g of H^0(C,omega_C) under (i/2)integral alpha wedge barbeta, define dmu_Ar=(i/(2g))sum_j alpha_j wedge baralpha_j. This probability form is independent of the chosen orthonormal basis.

items.name: Archimedean admissible metric
items.statement: Let C be a compact Riemann surface of genus g>0. A smooth hermitian metric on L is admissible when c1(L,||.||)=deg(L)dmu_Ar. On C×C require this condition on the restriction to each horizontal and vertical fiber.

items.name: Archimedean admissible Green function
items.statement: Let C be a compact Riemann surface of genus g>0. A Green function g_D for a Cartier divisor D is smooth off D with g_D+log|f| smoothly extending in a local meromorphic equation div(f)=D. It is admissible if its metric ||1||=exp(-g_D) on O(D) has Chern form deg(D)dmu_Ar; equivalently (i/pi)partial barpartial g_D=deg(D)dmu_Ar-delta_D with the paper differential convention.
items.note: The displayed PDE on p.102 omits deg(D); the preceding Chern-form definition implies the factor. The corrected general equation is recorded explicitly; for D=x it agrees literally with the printed equation. items.name: Existence and uniqueness of complex admissible metrics
items.statement: Let C be a compact Riemann surface of genus g>0. Every line bundle on C, and every line bundle on C×C with the fiberwise admissibility condition, has an admissible metric unique up to multiplication by a positive constant.

items.name: Normalized Arakelov Green function
items.statement: Let C be a compact Riemann surface of genus g>0. There is a unique symmetric Green function g_Ar on C^2\Delta, smooth off the diagonal with the specified logarithmic singularity, such that g_Ar(x,.) is admissible for O(x) and integral_C g_Ar(x,y)dmu_Ar(y)=0 for every x. It defines the admissible diagonal metric by ||1||=exp(-g_Ar).

items.name: Arakelov dualizing metric
items.statement: Let C be a compact Riemann surface of genus g>0. The Arakelov metric on omega_C is the unique smooth metric making the residue map (omega_C⊗O(x))|x→C an isometry for each x, with O(x) carrying the normalized Green metric and C the ordinary absolute value. It is admissible.

items.name: Symmetric diagonal metric
items.statement: Let K be complete with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0. A continuous metric on O(Delta) over (C^2)^an is symmetric if its Green function -log||1|| on the complement of Delta^an is invariant under the transposition of C×C. For x∈C(K′) over finite K′/K its pullback along (x,id) gives a metric on O(x) over C_K′.

items.name: Canonical nonarchimedean admissible metric pair
items.statement: Let K be complete with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0. There exists a unique pair of metrics on omega_C and O(Delta), both integrable and the diagonal metric symmetric, with these properties for every finite extension K′/K and x,y∈C(K′): c1(O(x))=c1(O(y)); c1(omega)=(2g-2)c1(O(x)); integral g_Delta(x,.)c1(O(x))=0; and the residue map (omega⊗O(x))|x→K′ is an isometry. These are the Zhang metrics.

items.name: Nonarchimedean Calabi uniqueness on curves
items.statement: Let K be complete with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0. items.name: Even and odd line bundles on an abelian variety
items.statement: For an abelian variety A over a field, a line bundle M is even if [-1]^*M≅M and odd if [-1]^*M≅M^{-1}. The theorem of the cube gives [2]^*M≅M^4 in the even case and [2]^*M≅M^2 in the odd case.

items.name: Admissible metric on an abelian variety
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K and M a line bundle on A. For even M a continuous metric is admissible when the isomorphism [2]^*M⊗M^{-4}≅O_A identifies its metric with a constant metric; for odd M replace4 by2. For general M require admissibility of the induced metrics on M⊗[-1]^*M and M⊗([-1]^*M)^{-1}.

items.name: Tate construction of abelian admissible metrics
items.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K and M a line bundle on A. Every M has an admissible metric on A^an unique up to a positive constant. It is integrable, and is semipositive when M is ample.

items.name: Curve admissibility through the Jacobian
items.statement: Let K be complete with a nontrivial nonarchimedean absolute value and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0. Choose alpha∈Pic^1(C), i_alpha:C→J and theta_alpha. A metric on L is admissible if for some positive m there is a line bundle M on J algebraically equivalent to an integer multiple of theta_alpha with an admissible metric, and an isometry L^m≅i_alpha^*M. If Pic^1(C) is empty, impose this after some finite extension where Pic^1 is nonempty.

items.name: Independence and existence of curve admissibility

items.name: Admissibility survives diagonal restriction

items.name: Admissible pairing with the diagonal

For an admissible metrized line bundle L on C and an admissible diagonal metric, the canonical isomorphism p1_*<O(Delta),p2^*L>≅L is an isometry up to a constant. items.name: Polarized reduction graph
items.statement: Let K be discretely valued and complete, with e_K=|uniformizer|^{-1}, and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0 with a K-point and split semistable reduction. Let Gamma be the dual graph of its minimal regular model, each edge of length1, and i:Gamma→C^an and r:C^an→Gamma the canonical inclusion and retraction. Vertices correspond to irreducible components, edges to nodes including loops. The canonical graph divisor is K_C=sum_v deg(omega_model|F_v)[v], of degree2g-2; each vertex additionally records the genus of the normalization of F_v.

items.name: Metric-graph Laplacian
items.statement: For a compact connected metrized graph Gamma with finite vertex subdivision, let F(Gamma) be the continuous functions that are C^2 on each open edge, with bounded second derivative there and finite one-sided directional derivatives. Define Delta f=-f′′dx-sum_P(sum_v d_v f(P))delta_P. It is a finite signed measure independent of subdivision and edge orientation.
items.note: Read [BF] Definitions 4–5 p.6. Its bounded-second-derivative function class avoids an unstated integrability assumption. [BR] §1.2 p.3 also gives the larger piecewise-C2, f′′∈L1 Zhang space; comparison of these domains is a separate extension. Use the common metric-graph Laplacian; analytic Green-potential extension is consumed by GZ.2.

items.name: Canonical graph measure and normalized Green function
items.statement: Let K be discretely valued and complete, with e_K=|uniformizer|^{-1}, and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0 with a K-point and split semistable reduction. Let Gamma be the dual graph of its minimal regular model, each edge of length1, and i:Gamma→C^an and r:C^an→Gamma the canonical inclusion and retraction. There is a unique probability measure mu_K, a finite combination of uniform edge measures and vertex point masses, for which the normalized Green function satisfies Delta_y g_mu(x,y)=delta_x-mu, integral g_mu(x,y)dmu(y)=0, and c+g_mu(K_C,x)+g_mu(x,x)=0 for a constant c independent of x. The kernel is continuous and symmetric.

items.name: Skeleton inclusion and retraction
items.statement: Let K be discretely valued and complete, with e_K=|uniformizer|^{-1}, and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0 with a K-point and split semistable reduction. Let Gamma be the dual graph of its minimal regular model, each edge of length1, and i:Gamma→C^an and r:C^an→Gamma the canonical inclusion and retraction. The metrized reduction graph canonically embeds in C^an and admits a canonical retraction from C^an; restriction of r to geometric points is the specialization used in the Green formula.

items.name: Explicit graph correction of the canonical metric
items.statement: Let K be discretely valued and complete, with e_K=|uniformizer|^{-1}, and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0 with a K-point and split semistable reduction. Let Gamma be the dual graph of its minimal regular model, each edge of length1, and i:Gamma→C^an and r:C^an→Gamma the canonical inclusion and retraction. Let ||.||_model be the metric from omega on the minimal regular model. Then ||.||_a(x)=||.||_model(x)e_K^{-c-g_mu(K_C,r(x))}=||.||_model(x)e_K^{g_mu(r(x),r(x))}.

items.name: Explicit graph formula for the diagonal Green function
items.statement: Let K be discretely valued and complete, with e_K=|uniformizer|^{-1}, and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0 with a K-point and split semistable reduction. Let Gamma be the dual graph of its minimal regular model, each edge of length1, and i:Gamma→C^an and r:C^an→Gamma the canonical inclusion and retraction. For distinct geometric points x,y, g_Delta,a(x,y)=(i(x,y)+g_mu(r(x),r(y)))log e_K, where i(x,y) is the normalized intersection of their sections after a finite extension defining them. The values extend uniquely to the analytic diagonal complement by continuity.

Let Gamma be the dual graph of its minimal regular model, each edge of length1, and i:Gamma→C^an and r:C^an→Gamma the canonical inclusion and retraction. For f∈F(Gamma), equip O_C with ||1||=e_K^{-r^*f}. PropositionA.4 identifies c1(O_C(f))=-i_*(Delta f) under its stated measure normalization.

items.name: Density of rational piecewise-linear model functions
items.statement: For the unit-edge reduction graph of a split semistable curve over a complete discretely valued field, rational subdivision points become components after suitable finite valued extensions and regularization. Rational-breakpoint piecewise-linear model potentials can approximate a piecewise-C2 potential uniformly with their Laplacian measures converging weakly, by approximating its finite signed Laplacian and applying the normalized Green operator.

items.name: Explicit admissible measure on the skeleton
items.statement: Let K be discretely valued and complete, with e_K=|uniformizer|^{-1}, and C/K smooth projective geometrically integral of genus g>0 with a K-point and split semistable reduction. Let Gamma be the dual graph of its minimal regular model, each edge of length1, and i:Gamma→C^an and r:C^an→Gamma the canonical inclusion and retraction. Let g_v be the normalization genus at v, delta_v its Dirac mass, delta_e the length measure of a unit edge, and r_e the resistance between its endpoints after removing its open interior. Then dmu_a=(1/g)i_*(sum_v g_v delta_v+sum_e (1/(r_e+1))delta_e). Interpret a bridge resistance as infinity, hence zero coefficient.

The polarized admissible graph measure and normalized Green kernel are explicitly owned here; this is not a second graph-theory plan.

items.name: Smooth relative curve

Let L1,...,L_{r+1} on X and M1,...,M_{m+1} on Y be integrable adelic bundles. For d=deg_{X_eta}(L1...Lr), psi_*<L1,...,Lr,psi^*M1>≅d M1.

items.name: Gross–Schoen self-height
items.statement: For the homologically trivial modified diagonal Delta_xi of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a global field, choose a regular model of C^3 on which its extension is numerically trivial on vertical fibers. items.name: Relative Bogomolov for the degree-positive Abel power over a function field
items.statement: Let k be a field and K a function field of one variable over k, with k the field of constants. Let S be a quasi-projective variety over K, and let pi : X -> S be a smooth relative curve of genus g > 1 which has maximal variation over k, that is, whose moduli morphism is generically finite on a projective model of S over k (equivalently, the family is not isotrivial after any base change to the constant field). Let alpha be a line bundle on X of positive degree on the fibres of pi. Then the S-morphism i_alpha^m : X^m/S -> J^m/S for any m >= dim S + 1 satisfies the relative Bogomolov conjecture of [DGH2, Conj. 1.2]: for a symmetric psi-ample line bundle L on the abelian scheme, rigidified along the identity, there is an epsilon > 0 such that the set of points of the source whose canonical height under the morphism is at most epsilon is not Zariski dense. The canonical height is the one attached to the adelic extension of L over k, not over K.
items.note: Theorem 4.19(1), function-field case, with the hypothesis corrected to maximal variation over the constant field k. As printed the hypothesis reads only 'maximal variation', which by the definition in section 1.6 is relative to the base ring, hence over K here; that form is false, and the counterexample is recorded as source issue PAPER-YUAN-26/E1. The number-field case is the separate item PAPER-YUAN-26/185, where the two readings agree. The paper's own proof of Theorem 4.19 states that it needs bigness 'over k instead of over K, where k = Z if K is a number field and k is the field of constants if K is a function field of one variable', which is what fixes the corrected hypothesis above.

items.name: Invertible sheaf on a scheme
items.statement: For a scheme X, an invertible sheaf is an O_X-module locally free of rank one. Tau Ceti packages the full subcategory of such modules; take isomorphisms when forming the paper’s Picard groupoid.
items.note: Actual declaration read at the pinned commit: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/LineBundle/Basic.lean:78.

items.name: Tensor product of invertible sheaves
items.statement: For invertible sheaves L,M on any scheme X, their sheaf tensor product is again invertible and is packaged as InvertibleSheaf.tensorProduct L M.

items.name: Abelian variety over a field
items.statement: An abelian variety over a field K is a proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K; smoothness, geometric connectedness and commutativity follow in the pinned library. This is a field-level object, not a relative abelian scheme.
items.note: Actual declaration read at the pinned commit: TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AbelianVariety/Basic.lean:94.

items.name: Number-field product formula
items.statement: For a number field K and x∈K nonzero, (product over infinite places w of |x|_w^{mult(w)}) times (finite-support product over finite places w of |x|_w) is 1.

items.name: Relative projective height substrate
items.statement: Over a field K with Height.AdmissibleAbsValues and a finite coordinate index, the relative logarithmic height of a point in Projectivization K (i→K) is the log of the product of local coordinate maxima; scalar invariance makes it well-defined. This does not include division by [K:Q] or extension invariance.

items.name: Bogomolov conjecture for curves
items.statement: For C a smooth projective curve of genus g > 1 over Qbar and alpha a divisor on C of degree 1, there is a constant c > 0 such that the set of x in C(Qbar) with hhat(x - alpha) <= c is finite, where hhat is the Neron-Tate height on the Jacobian J of C. Proved by Ullmo.
items.note: The classical statement that this paper's Theorem 1.1 makes uniform in the curve. Planned by RP.5, which asks for 'a separate Bogomolov/small-points theorem for subvarieties of abelian varieties over number fields' and names Ullmo/Zhang as the primary source to pin.

items.name: Equidistribution of small points
items.statement: The equidistribution theorem of Szpiro-Ullmo-Zhang for sequences of small points, which is the basis of Ullmo's proof of the Bogomolov conjecture for curves.
items.note: Quoted as the input to [Ull]; this paper does not use it, its own route to uniform Bogomolov going through adelic bigness instead. DY.4 'Equidistribution and small points' plans the primary equidistribution theorem for semipositive adelic metrized line bundles, and RP.5 requires 'the selected primary equidistribution proof' to be supplied.

items.name: The new gap principle
items.statement: There are constants c_1, c_2 > 0 depending only on g > 1 such that for any smooth projective curve C over Qbar of genus g and any y in C(Qbar), the number of x in C(Qbar) with hhat(x - y) <= c_1 max{h_Fal(C), 1} is at most c_2, where h_Fal(C) = h_Fal(J) is the stable Faltings height of the Jacobian. This is [Gao3, Thm. 4.1], a combination of [DGH1, Prop. 7.1] and [Kuh, Thm. 3].
items.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, section 1.1, p. 4; [Gao3] Theorem 4.1, [DGH1] Proposition 7.1, [Kuh] Theorem 3
items.note: The statement this paper's Theorem 1.1 strengthens and generalizes, in three respects that the paper lists: an extra non-negative term hhat((2g-2)alpha - omega) in the bound, alpha allowed in Pic^1(C_Kbar) rather than only in C(Kbar), and validity over global fields of every characteristic with constants uniform across them. The paper's proof is independent of it and does not use the non-degeneracy of the Faltings-Zhang map on which [DGH1, Kuh] crucially depend.

items.name: Uniform Manin-Mumford for curves as the degenerate case
items.statement: The case c_1 = 0 of the new gap principle is a uniform version of the Manin-Mumford conjecture for curves: the number of torsion points of the form x - y, for x in C(Qbar), is bounded by a constant depending only on the genus. DeMarco-Krieger-Ye had previously proved the new gap principle in the case g = 2 with y a Weierstrass point and C admitting a degree-two morphism to an elliptic curve.
items.note: Recorded because the paper states it as the content of the c_1 = 0 specialisation and because it fixes what is and is not new in [DGH1, Kuh]. RP.5 plans the non-uniform Manin-Mumford route; the uniform bound is a quantitative strengthening that it does not plan.

items.name: Upper bound on the number of points of large height
items.statement: The proofs of the Mordell conjecture by Vojta, its extension to the Mordell-Lang conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties by Faltings, and Bombieri's simplification in the case of curves, all give an upper bound on the number of points of large height on the curve; the bound was further refined by de Diego and by Remond.
items.note: The complement of the gap principle: the gap principle bounds the small points and this bounds the large ones, and it is the combination of the two that yields the uniform Mordell-Lang bound. The paper uses it only to state that consequence, its own contribution being the small-point half.

items.name: Uniform bound for Mordell-Lang on curves
items.statement: There is a constant c > 0 depending only on g > 1 such that for any smooth projective curve C of genus g over an algebraically closed field F of characteristic 0, any y in C(F), and any subgroup Gamma of J(F) of finite rank, the number of x in C(F) with x - y in Gamma is at most c^{1 + rank Gamma}. This is [Kuh, Thm. 4], obtained by combining the large-height upper bound with the new gap principle; it answers the uniform Mordell-Lang problem proposed by Mazur.
items.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, section 1.1, pp. 4-5; [Kuh] Theorem 4, [Maz] p. 234
items.note: The headline consequence of the uniform Bogomolov circle of ideas, and the reason the paper's Theorem 1.1 matters beyond its own statement: substituting Theorem 1.1 for the gap principle gives an alternative proof of this bound, one that avoids o-minimality and extends to function fields of arbitrary characteristic. RP.5 plans the qualitative Mordell-Lang route, not this uniform quantitative form.

items.name: Boundary growth of the phi-invariant from graph data
items.statement: A more detailed analysis of the proof of Theorem 3.10 describes the growth of the phi-invariant along the boundary of the moduli space of complex curves in terms of the graph-theoretic data encoded by the adelic divisor Phi-tilde. Song's recent work goes in this direction and confirms a variant of a conjecture of de Jong.
items.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, Remark 3.11, p. 59; [Son], [dJo2] Conjecture 1.2
items.note: Asserted as a consequence of the paper's own method rather than proved. Recorded because it says what the proof of Theorem 3.10 yields beyond the positive lower bound the theorem states, and because it is the archimedean half of the pair completed by Remark 4.13(2).

items.name: The epsilon- and delta-invariants cannot be globalized
items.statement: Since the epsilon-invariant has a non-trivial non-archimedean component but a trivial archimedean one, it cannot be globalized in the sense of the preceding construction; and therefore neither can the delta-invariant.
items.note: A negative result, and the reason the globalization used for Phi_S is not available for these two invariants: it delimits the method of section 4.5.2 and a design job must not assume an analogous adelic divisor exists for epsilon or delta.

items.name: Boundary growth of the Faltings delta-invariant from graph data
items.statement: Running the argument of Remark 3.11 with the adelic divisor Xi in place of Phi shows that the growth of Faltings' archimedean delta-invariant along the boundary of the moduli space of curves is controlled by the graph-theoretic data of the non-archimedean invariant delta + epsilon. This partially explains the results of de Jong and of Faltings on that growth.
items.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, Remark 4.13(2), p. 91; [dJo4] Theorem 1.1, [Fal4] Theorem 7
items.note: The delta-analogue of item 278, and the payoff of the Xi-globalization of section 4.5.2. Asserted as a consequence of the method rather than proved.

items.name: Numerical bound on the coefficient A(g)
items.statement: With A(g) = 1 + (3/(2c(g)) + 2)(2g+1)/(g-1) built from Cinkir's constants, one has A(g) <= 139 < 144 for every g > 2; the genus-2 case instead uses the hyperelliptic improvement, with coefficient 107.25. Since Cinkir's c(g) tends to 1/14 as g grows, the coefficient 12/A(g) tends to 12/47.
items.locator: Author manuscript 21 August 2024, section 4.5.1, pp. 87-88, with Remark 4.12(1), p. 88
items.note: Split off from item 158, which bundled two distinct things: the constants c(2) = 1/27, c(3) = 17/288, c(4) = 3/88 and c(g) >= 1/25 for g >= 5 in Cinkir's inequality phi(Gamma) >= c(g) delta(Gamma), which are imported, and the numerical bound on A(g) derived from them here, which is this item. Item 158 now carries only the imported constants.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 4.19, p. 101, read together with the definition of maximal variation in section 1.6, p. 16 (author manuscript dated 21 August 2024; identical in arXiv:2108.05625v4)
sourceIssues.printed: Theorem 4.19. Let K be either a number field or a function field of one variable. Let S be a quasi-projective variety over K. Let pi : X -> S be a smooth relative curve over S of genus g > 1 with maximal variation. [...] Then the following morphisms satisfy the relative Bogomolov conjecture: (1) the S-morphism i^m_alpha : X^m_{/S} -> J^m_{/S} for any m >= dim S + 1. [...] -- where section 1.6 defines: "Let S be a quasi-projective integral scheme over a noetherian base ring R [...] We say that pi : X -> S has maximal variation (or maximal variation of moduli) if the moduli morphism S -> M_{g,R} associated to pi is generically finite"
sourceIssues.correction: In the function-field case the hypothesis must be maximal variation over the field of constants k, not over K: the moduli morphism must be generically finite on a projective model of S over k, equivalently the family must not become isotrivial over the constant field. The number-field case needs no change.
sourceIssues.reason: As stated the theorem is false in the function-field case. Because S is a quasi-projective variety over K, the base ring in the section 1.6 definition is R = K, so 'maximal variation' means that S -> M_{g,K} is generically finite. Take k any field, K = k(t), and S = Spec K, so that dim S = 0. Let C be a smooth projective curve of genus g >= 2 over k and let X = C x_k K be the constant family, with alpha any line bundle of positive degree. The hypothesis is then satisfied vacuously: S = Spec K is its own dense open and Spec K -> M_{g,K} is quasi-finite, so the family has maximal variation over K. Part (1) with m = 1 >= dim S + 1 therefore asserts the relative Bogomolov conjecture for i_alpha : X -> J. But that fails: by the definition recalled on p. 100 the canonical height is the one attached to the adelic extension of L over k, and every point of C(kbar), viewed in X(Kbar), is a constant section of a constant family and so has canonical height 0; C(kbar) is infinite, hence Zariski dense in the curve X_{Kbar}. So for every epsilon > 0 the set of points of height at most epsilon is Zariski dense, contradicting the conclusion. The defect is only in the hypothesis, and the paper's own proof shows what the hypothesis should be: it states 'Similar to Proposition 4.18, we need the bigness of the adelic line bundles over k instead of over K, where k = Z if K is a number field and k is the field of constants if K is a function field of one variable', and the bigness input it invokes, Theorem 4.5, requires maximal variation over that same k. Proposition 4.18, on p. 100, is stated correctly and carries bigness on S/k as an explicit hypothesis; it is Theorem 4.19 that fails to upgrade 'maximal variation' to match. The number-field case is unaffected: there k = Z, and for S a variety over a number field K generic finiteness of S -> M_{g,K} is equivalent to that of the induced morphism on a Z-model, since passing to the model adds one to the dimension of the source and of the image alike. Consistently with this, the paper's main uniform theorem is stated with an explicit non-isotriviality condition of its own (section 4.3.2), so the isotrivial case is excluded there and that theorem is not affected.

sourceIssues.printed: If C has split semistable reduction, delta(C) is also the total number of nodes on the minimal regular model of C over O_K; in general, if K' is a finite extension of K such that C has split semistable reduction over K', then delta(C) = delta(C_{K'})/[K' : K]

sourceIssues.reason: False as printed, and the two halves of the one sentence contradict each other. Let C already have split semistable reduction over K and let K'/K be unramified of degree f > 1. By the first half, delta(C) is the number of nodes of the minimal regular model over O_K. Over O_{K'} the reduction is still split semistable and the minimal regular model base-changes etale-locally, so it has the same nodes and delta(C_{K'}) = delta(C). The second half then gives delta(C) = delta(C)/f, forcing delta(C) = 0 for every such curve. The recipe is not even well defined as printed, since taking K' = K and K' unramified quadratic give answers differing by a factor 2. With the ramification index it is consistent: a node with local equation t_1 t_2 = pi^m becomes t_1 t_2 = pi'^{em} after a degree-e ramified extension, so delta scales by exactly e. That delta is the raw uniformizer-normalized length, with no residue-degree factor, is fixed by the paper's own conventions: p. 47 normalizes the local Green functions by log e_v, and section 4.5.1, p. 86, writes the global invariants as delta(C) = deg(Delta_S) and phi(C) = sum_v phi_v(C) deg(v), carrying the residue degree separately in deg(v). sourceIssues.locator: Section 1.6, p. 16 (definition of a stable curve)
sourceIssues.printed: The curve is called stable if it is semistable with arithmetic genus g > 1, and any rational irreducible component of C_kbar intersects other irreducible components at three or more points
sourceIssues.correction: any SMOOTH (nonsingular) rational irreducible component, as in Deligne-Mumford Definition 1.1(iii)
sourceIssues.reason: As printed the definition excludes genuine stable curves. Take C over kbar irreducible and rational with exactly two nodes, both self-intersections. It is reduced with only ordinary double points, so semistable by the paper's own definition, and its arithmetic genus is 0 + 2 = 2 > 1. It is a stable curve in the standard sense - its only component is singular, so the Deligne-Mumford condition on nonsingular rational components is vacuous, and omega_C is ample - and it is a point of the boundary of Mbar_2. But its unique component is rational and meets OTHER irreducible components in 0 < 3 points, so the printed condition fails. The paper treats its own section 1.6 and [DM, section 1] as interchangeable, saying on p. 41 'We refer to [DM, Sec. 1] (or our Sec. 1.6) for quick definitions of stable curves', and then defines Mbar_g as the moduli of stable curves, whose boundary contains exactly the curves the printed definition rules out. Section 3.3.4 confirms the intended notion by counting nodes 'of type 0', where the partial normalization is connected, i.e. self-nodes of a single component. Every later use is the Deligne-Mumford notion, so nothing downstream is affected.

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 2.3, p. 28, with its proof in section 2.2.3, p. 32
sourceIssues.printed: Let pi : X -> S be a smooth relative curve of genus g > 0. [...] (a) There is an adelic line bundle omega_{X/S,a} [...] Moreover, omega_{X/S,a} is nef and unique up to isomorphism
sourceIssues.correction: the proof establishes this only for g > 1; for g = 1 both the normalization and the nefness are unproved
sourceIssues.reason: The stated hypothesis is g > 0 but the proof supports only g > 1, in two independent ways. First, the normalization: section 2.2.3 pins down beta-bar_2, and hence O(Delta)_a, by an isomorphism whose coefficient is (2g-2), which vanishes at g = 1, so the condition it is meant to impose becomes vacuous and neither beta-bar_2 nor beta-bar_1 is determined. Second, the nefness asserted in (a) is proved nowhere for g = 1: the only proof of nefness in the paper is Theorem 2.10(1), whose formula carries 1/(4g(g-1)) and is meaningless at g = 1, and Theorem 2.10 opens by assuming g > 1. The paper itself notices the mismatch without resolving it, remarking on p. 40 'Note that we require g > 1 in this section, while we only require g > 0 in the previous section.' A repair is available inside the paper's own toolkit, since the condition used in section 3.3.3 has coefficient 2 - 1 = 1 and so survives g = 1. The g = 1 case of Proposition 2.7 and Theorems 2.8 and 2.9, which rest on Theorem 2.3 under the same standing hypothesis, is affected in the same way; every application in sections 3 and 4 has g > 1.

sourceIssues.printed: The proof is similar to (3), as Theta|_Y is ample on the generic fiber of Y -> S

Remark 4.15(2), the Northcott property of omega^2_{C/K,a} (item /170), rests on [FC, Chap. V, Prop. 4.6] - Faltings-Chai, Degeneration of Abelian Varieties - for the Northcott property of Faltings heights of abelian varieties with semistable reduction over number fields, and on Torelli's theorem to transfer it to curves. Neither this session nor the two earlier ones read that proposition, so the precise form of the quoted input is unverified: in particular whether it is stated for a fixed number field or for varying fields of bounded degree, and over which quotient the finiteness holds. The item is recorded with the geometric reading made explicit, which is the reading the cited inputs support and the one Pazuki's theta-height Northcott theorem is stated for, but the primary statement must be recovered before the finiteness is planned. Do not convert it into finiteness of isomorphism classes over one fixed K without a separate finiteness-of-twists argument.

The local comparison between the unit-edge-length reduction graph and the fixed-absolute-value skeleton was settled for split reduction by the earlier continuation of this job: with lambda_K = log e_K the two differ by scaling all lengths by lambda_K, the Laplacian transforms as Delta_log F = s_* Delta_unit f, and the Chern-measure comparison carries no extra scalar on model-degree mass. What is still open is the general case: geometric residue-orbit weights for nonsplit reduction, compatibility with arbitrary models and with resolution, and the general descent comparison. Raw intersection lengths, residue-weighted degrees and geometric base change must be kept distinct - an unramified extension with residue degree f > 1 is the negative control against dividing a raw length by the full degree [L:K], and a ramified regular node gives e subedges of logarithmic length lambda_K/e. Controlled approximation is also still needed for arbitrary continuous metrics, since uniform convergence alone does not control Laplacians.
